learningObjectives: Distinguish between a data object (structure) and a data record (instance)
Explain the role of Data Pages as a virtualization layer
Separate generated Data Page defaults from structure, edit mode and scope
Use the Integration Designer to view and manage data objects and integrations

elements.description: A structure that groups related fields to describe a business entity (e.g., Customer with Name, Email, Phone). Reusable across all Case Types. In Dev Studio, a data object is called a data type and a field is a property.

elements.text: A Pega data model is like a factory's inventory system: Data Classes are the warehouse shelves (organized by type), Data Records are the physical items (actual data instances), and Data Pages are the forklifts — they retrieve items from wherever they are stored (local warehouse or external supplier) and bring them to the production floor, caching the load for reuse according to scope, parameters and refresh configuration.

elements.description: A well-designed Data Model promotes reuse, accuracy, consistency, and scalability. You model the data an application needs to complete work, then connect it to Case Types so the workflow has the right data at the right time.

Data for a data object can be stored LOCALLY in the Pega database, or sourced from an EXTERNAL system of record (e.g., a client database or web service). Pega ships pre-configured objects (e.g., Address-Postal, Address-Email) to reuse or extend.

Conceptual: business entities, attributes and relationships. Logical: translate them into Pega data objects and fields. Physical: storage and integration details. Treat the conceptual model as evolving; involve stakeholders and have the LSA review the design before creating objects.

elements.description: The unique set of fields and values for one instance of a data object (e.g., one Customer = Ian / Mitchell / email / phone). Records live in a system of record — Pega DB or external.
Two types of data model changes with different implications:
items: VALUE change (add a customer, update a phone number) — normal business operation; no process change needed
STRUCTURE change (adding/removing fields) — modifies the data object definition; requires careful planning

elements.description: Use the Records tab for data configured to local Pega storage. Inspect its configured keys; a generated identifier such as pyGUID is not a workflow status. Do not assume every data object or external source uses the same identifier.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Data Pages and the Visual Data Model

elements.description: The bridge between a data object and its data — retrieves from a source and CACHES it in Clipboard memory. Hides integration details so developers work with sourced data without knowing where it lives.

elements.term: Pega Live Data & default Data Pages
elements.description: Data Pages separate application data usage from integration. The source describes three defaults for data objects configured to a system of record: single read, list read and a save page. These generated defaults are not the general taxonomy: Page/List structures, Read-only/Editable/Savable modes, and Thread/Requestor/Node scopes are separate settings.
A simulated source is temporary for development and testing. Connect and validate the final source before production; a diagram showing the object does not establish that its integration is ready.
The Visual Data Model shows objects and their relationships and supports field changes. Inspect configured cardinality rather than inferring physical foreign keys from a diagram.

elements.title: Data Model Design Decisions

elements.term: Data objects and Integrations landing page
elements.description: The Integration Designer is the single place in App Studio to see the application's data objects, their Data Pages, the systems of record (SOR) that source them, which Case Types reference each object (Referenced By), and simulated data sources.
From the Integration Designer you open the Visual Data Model (objects and relationships) and the Integration Map (a diagram of data objects and the systems of record from which they are sourced).

examPitfalls.title: Data object = data type; field = property
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions use 'data object' and 'data type' interchangeably and ask candidates to match them to Pega terms. Candidates select different answers. Data object = Data Type (App Studio) = Class (Dev Studio); field = Property — all are the same concept in different contexts.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: When a scenario switches between studios, translate on the fly: App Studio 'data object/field' equals Dev Studio 'Data Type/Property' — same artifact, different label.

examPitfalls.title: Value change vs. structure change
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what happens when a property's data type changes from Text to Integer. Candidates say the data is automatically converted. Changing a property's data type is a structural change — existing stored data may be lost or corrupted; a migration is needed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Value changes affect records; field changes affect the definition. Assess consumer and migration impact rather than assuming every change requires a workflow change.

examPitfalls.title: pyGUID is for local records
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A generated record identifier is separate from a Case ID or Case status. Verify configured keys instead of assuming pyGUID universally.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use the actual data-object key configuration for record identification.

examPitfalls.title: Generated defaults are not all page types
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The topic describes three defaults for objects configured to a system of record. Do not confuse their read/save responsibilities with Page/List structure, edit mode or scope.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect the generated pages in the application; treat their count as a configured pattern.

examPitfalls.title: Data Page caches in memory
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Cached Data Page values are separate from persistent source records. Cache visibility and lifetime depend on scope, parameters and refresh policy; Editable alone does not supply a save plan.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Data Page = bridge/cache; the SOR is where data is actually stored.

examPitfalls.title: Relationship indicators
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Cardinality describes one or many related records. Relationship notation does not determine physical database storage or replace inspecting the Field Type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Read the Visual Data Model icons carefully for cardinality questions.

examPitfalls.title: Integration Designer purpose
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The Integration Designer (Data objects and Integrations landing page) is the central view of objects, Data Pages, SORs, and dependencies — not a UI builder.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: If a question asks where to see all data objects + their SORs + which Cases use them, it's the Integration Designer.

examPitfalls.title: Local vs external storage
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Local records live in Pega DB tables (Records tab); external records are rows in a client system fetched via integration/Data Pages.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Add locally via Records tab; for external, each row is a record retrieved at runtime.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA defines a 'Customer' data object in App Studio grouping First name, Last name, Email, and Phone. When the SA opens the same construct in Dev Studio, what is the technical term for it and its data elements?

options.text: A data type (class), whose data elements are properties
A data object, whose data elements are properties — the term 'data type' only appears in the Visual Data Model, not Dev Studio
A data type, whose data elements are embedded data objects — each field in a data type is itself a smaller data object
A Data Page, whose data elements are records — the Data Page defines the data structure and its cached rows

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio calls it a 'data object'; Dev Studio uses the technical class term.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A data type/class describes the Customer structure and properties describe its fields. A Data Page loads values; a record is an instance. The class definition is not a cached record.

optionExplanations.A: The data object corresponds to a data type/class and its fields to properties.
optionExplanations.B: This preserves the wrong terminology distinction between the two Studios.
optionExplanations.C: Fields can be primitive properties; they are not all embedded objects.
optionExplanations.D: A Data Page loads instances of a type rather than defining the type itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Customer' data object has fields for First name, Last name, and Email. The application holds 1,000 customers. What does a single Data Record represent?

options.text: The unique collection of field values for one specific customer instance — e.g., John Smith, jsmith@co.com
The definition of the fields (First name, Last name, Email) shared by all customers — the structural template
A cached Data Page loaded in memory when the Case opens
A relationship link container connecting two data objects

practiceQuiz.hint: 1,000 customers = 1,000 Data Records; the field definitions are the data object itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Data Record is the collection of values for one specific instance of a data object — one customer's name and email. Fields define the structure; Data Pages fetch and cache data — neither is an instance.

optionExplanations.A: One record contains the field values for one particular customer.
optionExplanations.B: The shared field definitions describe the type rather than an individual record.
optionExplanations.C: The cache can hold a record, but it is not the record identity or definition.
optionExplanations.D: A relationship links data rather than representing this customer instance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA adds a new Data Record for 'Maya Chen' in the Records tab. After saving, a system-generated value called 'pyGUID' appears. What is pyGUID?

options.text: An automatically assigned unique identifier stored with the Data Record that allows it to be retrieved later
The customer's email address, used as the unique identifier by Pega to look up the record
The current status of the Case associated with this customer record
A test flag that marks the record as simulated data rather than production data

practiceQuiz.hint: 'py' prefix = Pega system property; GUID = globally unique identifier.
practiceQuiz.rationale: pyGUID is the auto-generated unique identifier assigned to a local Data Record — it allows the record to be retrieved and associated with the correct Case. It is system-generated, not user-supplied.

optionExplanations.A: pyGUID provides the generated identifier for this locally created record.
optionExplanations.B: An email value is not the generated pyGUID even if another design uses email as a key.
optionExplanations.C: Case status describes workflow state rather than the customer record identifier.
optionExplanations.D: pyGUID does not indicate whether a record is simulated or production data.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Product data object is configured for local Pega storage. An SA needs to enter test records without direct database access. Where can these records be added?

options.text: The Records tab — enter local records in the Pega-managed store
The Integration Map — the map interface allows direct record insertion into any connected data source
Dev Studio only — local Data Records can only be created through the Rules layer via Dev Studio, not the application UI
The Pulse feed — record creation is performed through the collaboration stream in the Pulse feed

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio provides a Records tab for adding local Data Records without database access.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Records tab supports local entry without direct database access. An external-source object is not automatically switched to local storage by adding records; inspect the configured source and keys.

optionExplanations.A: The Records tab supports local data record entry into the Pega-managed store.
optionExplanations.B: The Integration Map describes sourcing rather than inserting records into any external database.
optionExplanations.C: Local record entry is not restricted to Dev Studio rule creation.
optionExplanations.D: Pulse supports collaboration, not the local Product Records entry interface.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team debates whether to build a custom 'VehicleInfo' data object for a claims app. A BA says: 'Just store everything in one big Text field — it's simpler.' An SA says: 'Pega ships pre-built objects we should check first.' Who is right and why?

options.text: The SA is right — Pega ships pre-configured data objects (e.g., Address-Postal, Address-Email) that teams should check for and reuse or extend before building from scratch, to avoid duplication and maintain consistency
The BA is right — a single Text field is simpler, faster to build, and Pega's model-driven UI renders it correctly regardless of the data structure
Both are wrong — Pega does not ship pre-built data objects; all objects must be created from scratch. The BA's suggestion is also wrong because Text fields cannot store structured data
The SA is right about checking existing objects, but if none match exactly, the team must always create from scratch — extending a pre-built Pega object is not supported

practiceQuiz.hint: Think: what does 'check the Pega-provided objects first' mean in practice?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pega ships pre-configured objects (like Address-Postal) that should be reused or extended before creating custom ones. Building a custom address object when one already exists creates unnecessary duplication.

optionExplanations.A: Review and extend suitable existing data structures before duplicating them.
optionExplanations.B: One unstructured string loses typed fields and useful model-driven behavior.
optionExplanations.C: Pega includes reusable data structures; the blanket absence claim is incorrect.
optionExplanations.D: Extension is possible; an exact match is not required before considering reuse.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA reviews the default Data Pages generated for a 'Product' data object configured to a system of record. How many Data Pages are created and of what types?

options.text: Three — a single read-only, a list read-only, and a single read-and-write (Savable) Data Page
Two — a single read-only and a list read-only (the same as a Case Type's defaults)
One — a single read-and-write Data Page used for both retrieval and save operations
Four — a single read-only, list read-only, single read-and-write, and a list read-and-write Data Page

practiceQuiz.hint: The stated system-of-record configuration generates separate read and save responsibilities.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For the described configured object, three defaults cover a single read, list read and save operation. The other counts do not match that pattern; it is not an exhaustive list of possible Data Page definitions.

optionExplanations.A: For a data object configured to a system of record, defaults cover single/list reads and a savable page.
optionExplanations.B: Two read pages omit the savable data-object page in this configured pattern.
optionExplanations.C: One page does not describe the separate generated read and save responsibilities.
optionExplanations.D: A list savable page is not part of the three-page default described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A conceptual data-model diagram explicitly marks both ends of the Student–Course relationship as many. What relationship does this represent?

options.text: Many-to-many — one Student can enroll in many Courses and one Course can have many Students
One-to-one — each Student has exactly one Course and each Course has exactly one Student
One-to-many — one Student has many Courses but each Course has only one Student
No relationship — multiple lines indicate disconnected nodes not yet linked

practiceQuiz.hint: Determine multiplicity at each end of the stated relationship.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Many at both ends means many-to-many. One-to-one restricts both ends; one-to-many restricts one end. This notation describes cardinality, not a missing connection or physical storage layout.

optionExplanations.A: Multiplicity at both ends represents students with many courses and courses with many students.
optionExplanations.B: One-to-one would restrict both ends to one related instance.
optionExplanations.C: One-to-many indicates multiplicity at only one end rather than both.
optionExplanations.D: The markers describe cardinality, not disconnected entities.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA opens the Integration Designer and finds the Integration Map. A team member asks: 'What is this map actually showing us?' Which description is correct?

options.text: A visual diagram of the application's data objects, their associated Data Pages, and the systems of record that source each object — the SA can see all integration dependencies in one place
A list of all the Access Roles in the application and which data objects each role can read or write
A flow diagram showing the sequence of Data Transforms that fire during the Case Life Cycle, linked to the data objects they modify
A dependency map showing which Rulesets reference which data objects, used for Ruleset version management

practiceQuiz.hint: Which tool shows data objects, Data Pages, and systems of record together?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Integration Map (in the Integration Designer) shows data objects, their Data Pages, and the systems of record that source them — the single view for data flow architecture. The Data Model shows fields and relationships.

optionExplanations.A: The map connects data objects, sourcing pages and their systems of record.
optionExplanations.B: Access Roles describe permissions rather than the Integration Map structure.
optionExplanations.C: A transform execution sequence is different from this data-sourcing map.
optionExplanations.D: Ruleset references are not the integration dependencies shown here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A 'Product' data object is sourced from an external inventory database. At runtime, Pega fetches products via integration. What does a single Data Record correspond to in this external context?

options.text: Each row in the external inventory table — one Data Record per database row retrieved via integration
The entire external database table — the table as a whole is a single Data Record
The Data Page cache in memory — the cached snapshot of data is the Data Record
The pyGUID column header — the column that stores unique identifiers constitutes a Data Record

practiceQuiz.hint: A Data Record is always a single instance — one row, one product.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For an externally sourced data object, each row in the external table is one Data Record. A Data Page fetches records; a Data Record IS an instance — the records live in the external system, not in the Data Page.

optionExplanations.A: Each returned inventory row represents one Product record in this example.
optionExplanations.B: The table contains many records rather than constituting one Product instance.
optionExplanations.C: A Data Page can cache the fetched rows; the cache is not a single record definition.
optionExplanations.D: A column name is metadata, not one complete inventory record.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA asks an SA to explain two key characteristics of data objects. Which TWO statements are correct?

options.text: Data objects group related fields to describe a single real-world entity such as Customer, Product, or Address
Data objects are reusable across multiple Case Types in the same application
A data object can store only one Data Record and cannot be reused across the application
A data object is the same artifact as a data relationship — both terms refer to the same Pega concept

practiceQuiz.hint: Two true statements about what a data object IS and what it CAN DO across Case Types.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Data objects group fields for a business entity and permit reuse across Case Types. A definition can represent multiple records; a relationship associates data rather than replacing the definition.

optionExplanations.A: A data object provides a structured definition for an entity and its fields.
optionExplanations.B: Case Types can reuse the same entity definition instead of duplicating it.
optionExplanations.C: An object definition can describe many records and be reused.
optionExplanations.D: A relationship associates data; it is not the object definition itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Customer data source changes from an internal database to a cloud API, while preserving the data contract used by the Case workflow. Which Pega capability separates source access details from the application's data usage?

options.text: Pega Live Data — a virtualization layer that separates business logic from the details of how and where data is accessed
A CI/CD pipeline — the automated build-and-deploy pipeline abstracts infrastructure so rule changes do not affect data sources
An Access Role — security roles enforce data access boundaries, ensuring the Case Life Cycle cannot be affected by source changes
A reporting dashboard — dashboards aggregate data independently so switching sources only affects reports, not the Case Life Cycle

practiceQuiz.hint: What Pega capability hides storage/access details from the business logic layer?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Live Data and Data Pages separate data usage from source access details. If the replacement preserves the required contract, the workflow can continue consuming the same data. Mapping, permissions, errors and integration behavior still require validation.

optionExplanations.A: Live Data separates application-facing data usage from the sourcing implementation.
optionExplanations.B: A deployment pipeline does not provide the runtime data abstraction.
optionExplanations.C: Permissions regulate access but do not map a changed source to the expected data shape.
optionExplanations.D: A reporting dashboard does not insulate the Case workflow from sourcing details.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A product manager asks to add a 'Loyalty Tier' field to the Customer data object. An SA says this is different from updating a customer's value. Why is adding a new field more significant?

options.text: Adding a new field changes the data object's structure — a design-time modification that may affect how Cases process and display the entity
Adding a field is the same as updating a value; both require only a runtime data-entry step with no design implications
The change only affects pyGUID reassignment and has no impact on the business process or existing records
Adding a field triggers a Data Page refresh but no structural change — Data Pages auto-update when new fields are added

practiceQuiz.hint: New field = structure change (design-time); updating a value = runtime operation.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Adding Loyalty Tier changes the definition, while updating a customer tier changes one record. Review consumers of the new field; this is not restricted to Dev Studio.

optionExplanations.A: A new Loyalty Tier field changes the schema and can affect consumers of Customer data.
optionExplanations.B: A value update changes an instance, not the entity structure.
optionExplanations.C: Adding a field does not inherently reassign every record identifier.
optionExplanations.D: Refreshing a page does not make a schema change equivalent to a record update.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A customer's shipping address changes. An SA proposes 'We need to update the data object structure to add the new address.' A lead SA immediately corrects them. What distinction is the lead SA making?

options.text: Adding a new address field is a structural change to the data object (design-time). Changing the address value for one customer is a data record operation (runtime). These are fundamentally different concerns
The SA is correct — all data changes in Pega, including customer address updates, require updating the data object structure in Dev Studio first
The distinction does not matter in Pega — structural and value changes both go through the same Records tab in App Studio
Address updates require a Savable Data Page change, not a data object change; the lead SA is correcting the wrong tool, not the wrong concept

practiceQuiz.hint: Changing a customer's ADDRESS VALUE vs adding a new ADDRESS FIELD to the object schema — which is which?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Updating an existing address changes record values. Adding an Apartment Number field changes the definition. App Studio can configure fields; a structural change is not inherently restricted to Dev Studio.

optionExplanations.A: Updating one address value changes a record; adding a field changes the schema.
optionExplanations.B: Routine record updates do not require a new type definition.
optionExplanations.C: The Records tab is not interchangeable with structural data-model design.
optionExplanations.D: A save mechanism may support the update, but the distinction is schema versus instance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA uses a simulated Data Page while the final Customer source is unavailable. What must happen before production?

options.text: Configure and validate the final data source before production
Leave the simulated source because generated pages guarantee production data
Delete every Data Page because simulation makes the model unusable
Rename the simulated page; no connection validation is needed

practiceQuiz.hint: Simulation enables development, not proof of a working production integration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Connect and validate the final data source before production. Simulation alone does not prove that source integration, mappings and permissions work.

optionExplanations.A: Replace the temporary source and validate the real integration.
optionExplanations.B: Generated pages do not make simulated values production-ready.
optionExplanations.C: The model can remain; its final source needs configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Renaming does not configure or validate the connection.

practiceQuiz.scenario: At runtime a user views Customer fields retrieved through a configured Data Page. Where does Pega hold the sourced values in memory?

options.text: On the Data Page — cached in memory under its configured scope and refresh policy
In the Ruleset — the Ruleset stores both the field definitions and their runtime values together
In the Access Role — the Access Role caches field values for the Persona to ensure consistent data across users
In the Pulse feed — the Pulse feed maintains the latest field values as collaborative updates streamed in real time

practiceQuiz.hint: Data Pages are the runtime home for data object field values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Data Page caches sourced values in memory. Visibility and reuse depend on scope, parameters and refresh configuration; the cache is distinct from the persisted source records.

optionExplanations.A: The sourced Customer values are held in an in-memory Data Page under its configured scope.
optionExplanations.B: Rulesets store rule definitions rather than these customer values.
optionExplanations.C: An Access Role defines authorization rather than storing customer field values.
optionExplanations.D: Pulse messages do not act as the data cache for the Customer object.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega System Architect is explaining the role of Data Pages to a junior developer. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Data Pages function in Pega?

options.text: Data Pages act as a virtualization layer between the application and its underlying data sources
Data Pages can cache data so that repeated calls to the same source within a session are avoided
Data Pages store rule definitions and replace Application Rulesets for data management
Data Pages are read-only by design and cannot write data back to any source system

practiceQuiz.hint: Data Pages virtualize data access and support caching — they are not rule storage or write-only constructs.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Data Pages provide a virtualization layer so the application accesses data through a consistent interface regardless of the underlying source (database, REST API, etc.). They support caching at configurable scopes (Thread, Requestor, Node) to reduce redundant source calls. Data Pages do not replace Rulesets and can be configured for both read and write operations.

optionExplanations.A: Data Pages separate the application data contract from source access details.
optionExplanations.B: Caching can reuse loaded data subject to scope, parameters and refresh configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Rule definitions remain in the rules infrastructure, not replacement Data Page storage.
optionExplanations.D: Savable Data Pages can execute configured save plans to the source.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is reviewing the Data Page scope types available in Pega. Which TWO are valid Data Page scope types that determine cache visibility?

options.text: Thread — cached data is visible within the current processing thread
Requestor — cached data is visible within the current requestor context
Global — data is permanently cached across all nodes and never invalidated
Database — data is stored in the Pega database and retrieved per request with no in-memory caching

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the three Pega Data Page scopes — Thread, Requestor, and Node — and what each covers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Thread and Requestor are valid scopes; Node is another supported scope. Scope determines visibility, while refresh and invalidation configuration also affect data lifetime. Global and Database are not the scope names.

optionExplanations.A: Thread scope makes a cached page available in the current processing thread.
optionExplanations.B: Requestor scope shares it within the requestor context, subject to refresh configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Node is a valid scope; permanent, never-invalidated Global is not.
optionExplanations.D: Database is a persistence location, not one of the Data Page cache scopes.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is using the Integration Designer to review the data architecture of a Pega application. Which TWO capabilities does the Integration Designer provide?

options.text: A visual map of all data objects and their relationships within the application
The ability to view and manage the integration connectors associated with each data object
A built-in SQL query editor for running queries directly against the Pega database schema
The ability to automatically generate machine learning models from the data object's field history

practiceQuiz.hint: Integration Designer maps data objects and their integrations — it does not run SQL or build ML models.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Integration Designer provides a visual overview of all data objects and their relationships, and allows the SA to view and manage the integration connectors (REST, SOAP, etc.) associated with each data object. It does not include a SQL query editor or machine learning model generation capabilities.

optionExplanations.A: The Integration Designer provides a visual overview of the data architecture.
optionExplanations.B: It supports inspecting and configuring the source integrations used for the objects.
optionExplanations.C: A general-purpose SQL editor is not the stated Integration Designer capability.
optionExplanations.D: Creating machine learning models is not the role of this integration map.

quickRecap.value: Groups related fields to model an entity; reusable across Case Types. = data type (Dev Studio); field = property.
Fields + values for one instance; stored locally (Records tab, gets pyGUID) or external (row = record).
Updating values changes records; adding or changing fields changes the definition and needs impact review.
Data Page: sourcing/cache abstraction. Objects configured to a system of record have three described defaults; structure, mode and scope are independent settings.
Visual Data Model shows objects and relationships; inspect single/list cardinality and Field Type.
Central view of data objects, Data Pages, SORs, and 'Referenced By'; links to Visual Data Model and Integration Map.
